pages.observed: Five samples 0.0 to 0.8 s of an illustrated airport curb at daytime. Phone card upper left reads Ride requested over a route map. White car partially visible at left edge of lane beside an outlined pickup bay. Blue airplane and car sign at right. Caption appears from 0.6 s reading Anyone in San Antonio can now hail a Waymo with no driver, in a dark box over the road. Lower half of frame is empty asphalt.

Samples 1.0 to 1.8 s. The full white car with a roof pod is now in frame, side profile, glides right into the outlined bay and stops with a red rear lamp glow by about 1.4 s. Car sits just above the caption box which covers the road below the bay. Phone card upper left unchanged reading Ride requested. Caption persists. Large empty asphalt below the caption.

2.0 to 2.2 s exterior: car stationary in pickup bay, locator card begins top right. At 2.4 s cut to a view from behind the front seats inside the cab: steering wheel left, dash nav screen right, windshield showing the airport sign and pale sky, two empty seat backs dominating the lower half. The empty driver seat is shown only as a seat back from behind. Wheel shows a small top marker; visible turning is slight across samples. Caption box overlaps the seat headrests. Phone card still reads Ride requested.

3.0 to 3.8 s interior cab view held. The steering wheel visibly rotates clockwise by a modest angle with no hands on it, while the airport sign slides out of the windshield to the right. Windshield otherwise mostly blank pale sky. Lower half of the frame is the two dark seat backs; driver seat emptiness is implied by no figure, seen only from behind. Texas outline card top right draws in. Phone card unchanged.

4.0 to 4.6 s cab interior held, wheel no longer turning, airport sign mostly out of windshield at right. Caption disappears at 4.6 s. At 4.8 s cut to an exterior curb shot: a large phone tilted in the lower left foreground reads Ride requested, Finding a car with a route map; the white car stands at the bay behind it at right; airport sign and canopy behind. Lower third of the frame is grey road bands.

5.0 to 5.8 s exterior curb with a large phone in the foreground covering the left half of the car. The marker on the phone map advances to the pin and the status flips from Ride requested to Arriving, At the curb by 5.6 s. The car is already parked and does not move in these samples. Caption reads the airport included. Texas locator rings a point in the south-central region.

6.0 to 6.6 s the curb shot holds with the phone at Arriving and the car parked; caption leaves after 6.0 s; nothing moves in 6.2 to 6.6 s. At 6.8 s cut to a new shot: a wooden table seen at an angle with a pale paper map sheet showing a faint grid, a few small round pins and green patches, and a small calendar card reading February at the far edge. No street names, river line or outline visible yet. Disclosure label still reads Generic car with no brand mark.

7.0 to 7.8 s the table and pale grid map hold almost static; the map content is very faint at phone size, with three tiny pins and two pale green blobs. At 7.6 s a thin blue river line begins to draw in from the top and faint gray street lines start. The February calendar card sits at the top edge of the table unchanged. Caption The service began in February sits over the lower table, below the map.

8.0 to 8.8 s map shot on the table holds. The blue river line completes from top to bottom, and thin gray streets and a faint ring road appear. Pins remain tiny. The February calendar card stays in place. The Texas locator card fades out at 8.0 s. The map occupies roughly the middle third of the frame; the top third is sky and the bottom third is table plank and caption.

9.0 s the wide table map holds. 9.2 s closer framing on the map sheet. From 9.4 s a tag reading 60 square miles, Limited area appears near the top and a February calendar page travels in from the right and lands on the lower map by 9.8 s. A dark outline stroke begins tracing from the upper left and is short at 9.8 s. Caption in a limited area of sixty square miles sits just under the map bottom edge.

10.0 to 10.8 s close map. A dark polygon outline traces clockwise from the upper left around the cluster of three pins and closes at 10.8 s, then fills with a translucent gray. Tag 60 square miles, Limited area sits above the outline; February calendar page sits at lower left. Caption in a limited area of sixty square miles sits just below the map. No car pin is distinguishable from the round pins at phone size.

11.0 to 11.8 s the completed outlined area holds as a gray-filled polygon over the map center, three small round pins inside drift slightly, tag and calendar unchanged. Caption unchanged. A completed-result hold of about one second.

12.0 to 12.2 s the outlined map holds with no caption. At 12.4 s cut to a creek: a wide sheet of brown water with a white car with roof pod already sitting in it, wheels hidden, its reflection below, trees with flat canopies on the far bank and stacked pale limestone ledges at lower right. The car moves leftward across the water between 12.4 and 12.6 s. Disclosure label changes to A different car, April 20th account. Rain is only faint streaks. The water surface reads as calm and flat. Caption appears at 12.8 s.

13.0 to 13.8 s the creek wide shot holds. The white car sits level, half submerged with its reflection, near the center of the water; it barely moves across these samples. Water surface flat brown with faint rain ticks and no visible current lines or waves. Cabin windows show pale seat shapes at phone size; occupancy is not clearly readable. Caption box sits on the water just below the car.

14.0 to 14.6 s creek wide shot with a slow drift; the car sits level and half submerged, a pale wake line now trails from its nose toward the right, limestone ledges slide away at right. At 14.8 s a closer framing: car larger near center, wake line at right, water flat brown with rain ticks. The car does not tilt, lift or rotate in these samples.

15.0 to 15.8 s medium framing on the car in brown water. From 15.2 s the car tilts slightly with its front raised and a front wheel showing, a brown mud line appears along the lower doors, a pale wake curls from the front to the right and small splash flecks show at the nose. The far-bank trees slide left between samples while the car holds near frame center. The tilt is modest; the car does not visibly rotate sideways. Cabin windows show seat shapes with no person.

16.0 to 16.8 s the car, slightly nose-up with a mud line and a wake at its front, slides leftward toward the left frame edge; trees shift with it. The motion reads as a slow sideways drift with the car still upright; there is no visible sideways lift or rotation. Caption ends after 16.4 s. Cabin seats visible through windows with no occupant.

17.0 to 17.2 s the creek car drifts out at the left edge. At 17.4 s cut to a flooded residential street: a beige single-story house, a tree and a green street sign behind a narrow band of brown floodwater in which a white car with a roof pod sits with water to its lower wheels. The bottom half of the frame is an empty pale paved foreground. Disclosure changes to Another car, earlier in April. A dark blob sits at the right edge of the water. Caption appears at 17.6 s over the water/pavement boundary just under the car.

18.0 to 18.8 s flooded street held. The brown water climbs on the white car from the lower wheels to above the wheel arches; by 18.4 s the wheels are mostly submerged. The car is small, about a quarter of frame width, in the upper-middle band. The lower half remains empty pale paving. Caption sits directly under the car, touching the waterline area. No amber lamp is visible in these samples.

19.0 to 19.6 s flooded street wide shot; the car stands still in water above its wheel arches and a small amber lamp at its front corner blinks on at 19.2 to 19.4 s. The lamp is a few pixels at phone size. At 19.8 s a closer framing: the car is larger, its windows show empty seat backs with no occupant, the background house and tree are softened, and the water is brown with a reflection. Caption remains below the car; the pale paved foreground still fills the lower third.

20.0 to 20.8 s medium-close of the stranded white car standing still in brown water to above its wheel arches, empty seats visible through the windows, background house and tree softened. Amber corner lamps blink on and off across samples. The car fills about two thirds of frame width in the upper-middle band; caption sits under its reflection; the bottom third is empty pale paving.

21.0 to 21.8 s the stranded car holds still in brown water with blinking amber corner lamps and empty seats through the windows. Caption leaves after 21.2 s. Nothing else changes; the lower third remains empty pale paving.

22.0 s last flood-street frame. At 22.2 s cut to a plain olive wall over a brown desk band. A cream card headed Federal recall record, Vehicle safety recall lies tilted across the desk, cropped off the right edge, with a dark pen at lower right. Card slides slightly left 22.4 to 22.8 s; a first short stroke appears on a ruled line at 22.8 s. Caption Waymo filed a software recall overlaps the card's lower left. Upper third and lower third are plain olive wall/floor.

23.0 to 23.8 s the record card slides into place and levels on the desk. Its rows write in: Recall type, Software, then Potential units affected with 3,791 by 23.6 to 23.8 s, with a text cursor bar following. The pen sits at the lower right corner of the card and does not travel along the text. Card occupies the middle third of the frame; upper and lower thirds are plain olive. Caption overlaps the lower card edge.

24.0 to 24.6 s the completed record card holds still on the desk with Software and 3,791 visible; caption gap at 24.6 s. At 24.8 s a new framing: card higher in frame, below it a grid of about forty small outlined car slots, with the first two filled by white car icons; a brown stamp handle edges in at right. New caption that could affect nearly thirty eight hundred cars sits over the lower grid.

25.0 to 25.8 s. Under the record card the grid of small white car icons fills row by row until all fifty slots are filled at 25.8 s. A forearm in a blue sleeve carries a wooden rubber stamp in from the right and moves it over the card's upper half, casting a shadow; it is still hovering at 25.8 s. The hand is a simple tan shape at the sleeve end; no fingers distinguishable at phone size. Caption sits below the grid.

26.0 to 26.8 s the hand lowers the wooden stamp onto the card's upper right, lifts it and withdraws to the right, leaving an orange Software recall imprint. Meanwhile a paper counter tag slides in under the card and settles reading Nearly 3,800 vehicles, 3,791 potentially affected in the record. The car-icon grid stays full. Contact and lift are both sampled; the imprint remains after the hand leaves.

27.0 to 27.8 s completed result hold: the stamped record card, the Nearly 3,800 vehicles tag and the full car-icon grid hold while the stamp hand exits right. Slight drift/scale change by 27.6 to 27.8 s. Caption leaves after 27.4 s. Lower third is plain olive.

28.0 s last record-card frame. At 28.2 s cut to a side-on road scene: grey multi-lane road with a dashed lane line, a lamp post, trees and skyline behind, a green verge below. The white car with roof pod enters from the left and advances right. By 28.8 s a cream card with the exact recall sentence fades in at the upper left. No standing water is yet visible on the road. Caption sits on the lower road edge just under the car. Lower third is plain green verge.

29.0 to 29.8 s tracking side view: the white car stays near frame left-center while the lane dashes, lamp post and trees scroll left, reading as forward travel. The recall sentence card holds at upper left. No standing water and no lit brake lamp are visible in these samples. Caption sits right under the car on the road edge; the bottom 45 percent of frame is flat green verge.

30.0 to 30.8 s the car's red brake lamp is lit and a flat pale grey-blue standing-water shape appears on the road at the right edge, closing toward the car, reading as the car slowing as it approaches water. The water is a smooth lozenge shape, partly hidden by the caption box's right end. The car stays at frame left-center. Recall sentence card unchanged; no word is highlighted yet.

31.0 to 31.4 s wide road: the car advances toward the standing-water shape ahead at right. At 31.6 s cut to a close side view: the car fills most of the frame width on a dark road, wheels and rims detailed, empty seats through windows, a thin pale wavy line at the tires; the recall card stays at top. At 31.8 s a pale water edge enters at the right ahead of the car and the caption becomes then drive into standing water on higher speed roads. The word may in the card is not yet highlighted.

32.0 to 32.8 s close tracking side view: the standing-water pool slides in from the right and its edge reaches the front tire by 32.8 s, reading as the car rolling into the water. At 32.8 s the word may on the recall card lights with a pale yellow highlight. Car shows empty seats. Caption sits just below the road; lower third is green verge with grass tufts.

33.0 to 33.8 s close tracking side view: the grey-blue standing water extends under the car, the front tire is in the water and pale ripple fragments appear at the front wheel by 33.6 to 33.8 s. The word may stays highlighted in amber on the recall card. The water reads as a flat tinted overlay on the road with small ripple marks rather than visible depth; no spray height above the tire.

34.0 to 34.8 s the car is in the standing water with diagonal wake streaks and reflections fanning behind its front tire; background tree and a lamp post scroll in at right, so the car is still moving forward through the water. The amber may highlight holds on the recall sentence card. Caption under the road; bottom third green verge.

35.0 to 35.4 s the car holds in the standing water with its wake and the highlighted may; caption absent. At 35.6 s cut to the desk with a tall record card carrying the earlier Software recall imprint, Recall type Software and Potential units affected 3,791; the card's lower half is blank. No remedy row is visible yet at 35.8 s. Caption The federal record says the remedy is currently under development appears at 35.8 s below the card.

36.0 to 36.8 s the record card's lower half fills: a Remedy row writes in with a peach highlight sweeping across, reading The remedy is currently under development by 36.4 s. A pen tip held by a small hand then enters from the right at row height and approaches the card; it has not touched the card at 36.8 s. Caption matches the row text below the card.

37.0 to 37.6 s a forearm in a blue sleeve rests a pen tip on the right end of the highlighted remedy row; the pen does not write or travel. At 37.8 s the framing tightens on the card and a second blue-sleeved forearm carrying a wooden stamp enters from lower right, the stamp below the remedy row, while the pen hand stays. Two separate arms enter from the right edge at once.

38.0 to 38.6 s the lower forearm presses a wooden stamp onto the card inside the remedy box below the text, while the upper forearm keeps the pen tip on the remedy row. At 38.8 s the stamp slides right revealing a partial orange imprint starting Und at the lower left of the remedy box. The two long arms cross diagonally from the right edge over the card. Card fills most of the frame width.

39.0 to 39.8 s the Under development stamp imprint sits complete and slightly tilted inside the remedy box below the remedy sentence. Both hands withdraw to the right: the stamp hand down and out, the pen hand back from the row. Caption leaves after 39.2 s. The completed record holds clean by 39.8 s.

40.0 s cut to a wide parking-lot row: four small white cars with roof pods side by side in angled stalls, a wire strung between two poles, an April calendar card on the left pole and a Vehicle maps card at right. From 40.4 s a tag reading Weather limits, tightened slides in from the left along the wire and pins near the left pole by 40.8 s. No cloud or rain icon visible on the tag at phone size. Cars occupy a narrow band across the middle; lower 45 percent is empty asphalt.

41.0 to 41.8 s the Weather limits, tightened tag, now showing a small cloud-and-rain icon, travels along the wire and pins near its center over the row of four parked white cars. Cars, April calendar and Vehicle maps card hold still. The tag is a small label at phone size; the row of cars is a thin strip. Lower half is empty dark asphalt with caption on it.

42.0 to 42.8 s the parking-lot wide shot holds. The only change is the Weather limits tag swinging a few degrees on its pin and settling. Cars, calendar and map card unchanged. Caption unchanged. This is the third consecutive second of the same composition after the tag arrived at about 41.4 s.

43.0 to 43.4 s the parking-lot shot holds unchanged. 43.6 to 43.8 s a slight push-in enlarges the scene. Caption changes at 43.8 s to and every affected car had the update by April twentieth. No car has a check mark and the calendar page shows only April with a blank sheet. From about 41.4 s to 43.8 s the frame shows no new event apart from the tag's small swing and this push.

44.0 to 44.8 s check-mark badges appear above each of the four parked cars in turn from left to right, each starting as a small dot and becoming a white circle with a dark check; all four are checked by 44.8 s. A small mark appears on the Vehicle maps card. The calendar still reads April with no day number visible. The badges are small, roughly a tenth of frame width.

45.0 to 45.8 s all four cars hold their check badges; the Vehicle maps card gains a check and a tiny updated label at 45.2 s. The April calendar still shows a blank page with no 20 visible. Otherwise static while the caption names April twentieth.

46.0 to 46.8 s the April calendar flips: blank page until 46.2 s, numeral 20 visible at 46.4 s, and by 46.6 s a flipped page hangs above the header. All four cars keep their check badges; Vehicle maps card shows updated with a check. The page flip lands after the checks, near the end of the clause.

47.0 to 47.6 s the parking-lot completed state holds: April 20 page, four checked cars, updated maps card; caption leaves after 47.0 s. At 47.8 s cut back to the airport curb: same canopy, bench, suitcase and airport sign as the opening; a white car with roof pod sits in the bay at right with its doors closed; phone card at upper left reads Arriving. Disclosure changes to A generic airport ride, not the flood cars. No caption at 47.8 s. Lower half is empty road with a dashed line.

48.0 to 48.8 s airport curb wide shot matching the opening composition. The parked white car's rear door swings open across the samples, showing a dark opening by 48.8 s. Car is small, about a third of frame width, sitting just above the caption. No person approaches. Phone card at upper left reads Arriving. Caption So the airport ride is open. Lower half is empty road.

49.0 to 49.8 s the curb shot holds with the car's rear door open, showing a beige door panel and dark interior; nothing else moves. Caption leaves after 49.6 s. At 49.8 s the lower road with dashed line is exposed, no caption. The same composition has held since 47.8 s, with only the door opening between 48.0 and 48.8 s.

50.0 to 50.8 s medium curb shot: the car waits at the bay with its rear door open; a phone lies propped on the bench. A small record card lies on the roadway below the car and slides toward the center, showing the remedy sentence and a tiny orange stamp; its text is small at phone size, about a quarter of frame width. Caption and the federal record lists the flood remedy appears at 50.2 s just below the card. The lower third is empty asphalt.

51.0 to 51.8 s the record card grows into the foreground below the car, its upper edge overlapping the car's wheels and the curb line; the remedy sentence and Under development stamp become legible. The car with its rear door open stays parked behind. The card floats over the road plane without a shadow or a surface it rests on. Caption directly below the card.

52.0 to 52.8 s the closing composition holds: the open-door car at the curb behind and the record card in the foreground reading The remedy is currently under development with its stamp. Only small card drift. Caption changes at 52.8 s to as currently under development. Lower 40 percent of the frame is empty asphalt.

53.0 to 53.8 s split frame: the airport curb with the open-door car fills the upper half; a brown desk fills the lower half with the record card and a small phone showing Arriving beside it. A dark underline draws beneath under development on the card across the samples. Caption as currently under development sits below the card. The curb and desk read as two stacked panels with a hard horizontal seam.

54.0 to 54.8 s the split closing frame holds: open-door car at the curb above, record card with the underlined remedy line and stamp plus a small phone below. Caption leaves after 54.0 s. No further movement in 54.2 to 54.8 s. The lower 45 percent of frame is empty brown desk.

55.0 to 55.8 s the split closing frame holds with no visible change and no caption: open-door car above, record card with underlined remedy text and stamp below, small phone at right. Continuous hold since about 53.8 s.

56.0 to 56.8 s cut to a dark credits card that fades in: THE DAILY DISPATCH header, Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, Visit the Docket texasaidocket.com with an arrow, then sources Waymo October 14th, NHTSA recall 26E026, Texas Public Radio May 10th and 13th, illustration and map notes, and the CC BY 4.0 music credit. Static after 56.2 s.
57.0 to 57.8 s the credits card holds unchanged: Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket, texasaidocket.com, sources, illustration, map and music credits on a dark background.
58.0 to 58.8 s the same credits card holds unchanged on a dark background with the Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com and the source and music credits.
59.0 to 59.8 s the credits card holds unchanged: Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket wordmark, texasaidocket.com, sources, illustration, map and music credits.
60.0 to 60.8 s the credits card holds unchanged with the Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket, texasaidocket.com and the source and music credits on a dark background.

Final phone frame 1829 at 60.967 s shows the same dark credits card: THE DAILY DISPATCH, Texas flag icon, Texas AI Docket, Visit the Docket texasaidocket.com, sources Waymo October 14th, NHTSA recall 26E026, Texas Public Radio May 10th and 13th, illustration, map and CC BY 4.0 music credit.
